content.thinking:
Alright, I've just completed the major overhaul: the UI now has a map picker, the CSS has been adjusted for responsive dialogs, the server startup script now assigns per‑entry ports, and the main game loop in main.js has been rewritten to wire everything together (renderer, game logic, HUD, netcode, etc.). The old `map.js` file was part of the previous architecture – it defined map data that is now fully represented in the new `maps.js` module and consumed by the rewritten main.js. Since `map.js` is no longer imported anywhere, it’s just dead code cluttering the repository.

Before I commit the changes, I need to make sure two things are true:
1. The obsolete `app/public/js/map.js` file is actually removed, so it won’t be served or cause confusion.
2. No other source files still contain an import like `from './map.js'`. If any remain, the build will break when the file disappears.

After confirming the removal, I also want a quick sanity check that the new `maps.js` module loads correctly and that each map object contains the expected properties (BOXES, LIGHTS, WAYPOINTS, DM_SPAWNS, and optionally a THEME). A simple Node script that imports `maps.js` and logs a summary for each map will give me that confirmation without having to spin up the full client.

I can do all of this in a single Bash command to keep the workflow atomic:
- `cd` into the `neonstrike` archive directory.
- `rm app/public/js/map.js` to delete the file.
- `grep -rn "from './map.js'" app/public/js/` to search the remaining JS files for any stray imports.
- Then run a one‑off Node command (with `--input-type=module` so I can use `import`) that dynamically imports `maps.js`, iterates over `MAPS`, and prints each map’s id together with counts of its arrays (`BOXES`, `LIGHTS`, `WAYPOINTS`, `DM_SPAWNS`) and whether a `THEME` is present.

If the `grep` returns nothing and the Node script prints sensible output for all maps, I can be confident the cleanup is complete and the new map data is well‑formed.

Thus the appropriate tool call is a Bash execution with exactly that command and a short description.

arguments.description: Delete old map.js, verify no imports remain, load maps.js
